from gurobipy import *

def solve_problem():
    m = Model("MultiObjective_Transportation")
    m.setParam('TimeLimit', 300)

    # --- Data ---
    I = 7  # sources
    J = 9  # destinations
    K = 3  # max suppliers per store
    w_cost = 0.6
    w_emission = 0.4

    supplies = [109, 248, 122, 85, 132, 184, 179]
    demands = [11, 31, 36, 12, 41, 51, 17, 56, 47]
    cost_matrix = [[4.53, 15.44, 9.42, 4.63, 23.56, 29.51, 26.84, 27.91, 15.32], [20.88, 25.58, 20.02, 24.67, 29.82, 16.93, 23.35, 23.91, 14.3], [5.77, 20.73, 9.17, 3.42, 3.02, 6.7, 27.64, 21.8, 3.81], [4.11, 21.92, 12.97, 28.82, 19.56, 26.81, 8.02, 7.7, 13.67], [5.66, 24.36, 9.62, 25.99, 6.32, 26.54, 10.74, 27.97, 19.0], [13.88, 9.91, 18.16, 26.98, 17.21, 25.75, 23.77, 24.04, 16.39], [6.74, 7.6, 8.93, 7.27, 27.96, 12.54, 12.46, 3.75, 24.29]]
    emission_matrix = [[7.81, 5.82, 13.85, 19.5, 16.46, 12.67, 4.9, 12.98, 6.73], [14.66, 2.47, 2.43, 3.8, 12.16, 15.11, 2.48, 17.07, 6.84], [5.9, 7.35, 19.83, 11.19, 6.34, 4.79, 1.0, 17.52, 19.63], [16.13, 16.98, 3.63, 11.36, 2.98, 5.25, 4.84, 20.0, 8.14], [16.71, 7.02, 13.53, 13.36, 17.3, 13.28, 4.05, 10.01, 12.29], [9.06, 7.06, 3.54, 12.66, 4.96, 16.42, 10.2, 14.27, 16.61], [10.27, 10.26, 8.63, 9.08, 10.47, 15.41, 5.36, 16.61, 6.12]]
    fixed_costs = [[224, 88, 107, 75, 138, 212, 129, 121, 296], [161, 251, 294, 138, 193, 164, 253, 120, 177], [186, 88, 250, 221, 199, 72, 74, 243, 131], [102, 255, 245, 293, 74, 136, 195, 155, 172], [128, 226, 295, 239, 167, 99, 251, 290, 255], [136, 51, 181, 294, 123, 138, 170, 142, 153], [298, 170, 80, 172, 101, 241, 300, 300, 271]]
    moq = [[6, 11, 10, 6, 6, 10, 6, 14, 17], [18, 7, 9, 6, 19, 17, 20, 12, 20], [17, 20, 5, 8, 16, 16, 13, 5, 6], [5, 5, 18, 17, 13, 13, 15, 10, 19], [7, 18, 5, 5, 20, 14, 18, 17, 16], [7, 18, 12, 6, 9, 8, 17, 10, 19], [19, 12, 12, 5, 8, 19, 7, 9, 19]]

    # Big-M per route
    total_demand = sum(demands)
    big_M = [[min(supplies[i], total_demand) for j in range(J)] for i in range(I)]

    # --- Variables ---
    # Continuous: shipment quantities
    x = {}
    for i in range(I):
        for j in range(J):
            x[(i,j)] = m.addVar(lb=0, vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name=f"Ship_S{i}_D{j}")

    # Binary: route-open indicators
    y = {}
    for i in range(I):
        for j in range(J):
            y[(i,j)] = m.addVar(vtype=GRB.BINARY, name=f"RouteOpen_S{i}_D{j}")

    # --- Objective ---
    # Weighted variable cost + fixed setup costs
    m.setObjective(
        quicksum(
            (w_cost * cost_matrix[i][j] + w_emission * emission_matrix[i][j]) * x[(i,j)]
            for i in range(I) for j in range(J)
        )
        + quicksum(fixed_costs[i][j] * y[(i,j)] for i in range(I) for j in range(J)),
        GRB.MINIMIZE
    )

    # --- Constraints ---
    # C1: Supply
    for i in range(I):
        m.addConstr(
            quicksum(x[(i,j)] for j in range(J)) <= supplies[i],
            name=f"Supply_S{i}")

    # C2: Demand
    for j in range(J):
        m.addConstr(
            quicksum(x[(i,j)] for i in range(I)) >= demands[j],
            name=f"Demand_D{j}")

    # C3: Linking — can only ship if route is open
    for i in range(I):
        for j in range(J):
            m.addConstr(
                x[(i,j)] <= big_M[i][j] * y[(i,j)],
                name=f"Link_S{i}_D{j}")

    # C4: Minimum order quantity
    for i in range(I):
        for j in range(J):
            m.addConstr(
                x[(i,j)] >= moq[i][j] * y[(i,j)],
                name=f"MOQ_S{i}_D{j}")

    # C5: Max suppliers per store
    for j in range(J):
        m.addConstr(
            quicksum(y[(i,j)] for i in range(I)) <= K,
            name=f"MaxSupplier_D{j}")

    m.optimize()
    return m

To: Supply Chain Leadership Team
From: Sustainability & Logistics Director
Subject: Balancing Cost and Carbon in Warehouse-to-Store Shipping with Practical Operating Rules
Date: Today

Context
We are moving product from multiple warehouses to multiple stores, and each shipping lane carries both a dollar cost per unit and a carbon impact per unit. In practice, the lowest-cost routes are often the most carbon-intensive. We need a plan that delivers product reliably while striking the right balance between financial performance and sustainability commitments.

Operational Rules
To reflect how our network actually works, the shipping plan must honor the following policies:
- Route activation costs: Any route we use carries a fixed setup charge that covers contracting, compliance, and dock preparation. A lane is either active or not, and the setup charge applies once a lane is activated, regardless of the volume shipped.
- Minimum order quantities on active lanes: If we activate a route, we must move at least a defined minimum number of units on that lane. This avoids partial loads and inefficient handling.
- Supplier limits per store: Each store can be served by no more than a defined number of warehouses to fit receiving capacity, vendor oversight, and contractual requirements.

Supply and Demand
Warehouse shipments cannot exceed available inventory, and each store must receive at least its required volume. The plan should use capacity where it is available and ensure every store’s need is covered.

Management Priority
Leadership has set explicit importance weights for cost and for emissions. In our planning, the per-unit cost and per-unit carbon will be blended using these weights. In addition, any activated route will carry its full setup charge. Said differently, the variable portion (dollars and carbon) is weighted according to management priorities, while fixed setup costs are added in full without weighting.

Business Goal
Recommend which routes to activate and how many units to ship on each active lane so that:
- We do not exceed warehouse inventory
- Every store’s demand is met
- Activated routes carry at least the required minimum volume
- Each store is supplied by no more than the allowed number of warehouses
- The blended total of variable shipping spend and total emissions, plus the full setup charges for any active routes, is as low as practicable under the above rules

This approach will allow us to quantify trade-offs between financial spend and carbon footprint, make transparent which lanes are worth activating, and ensure the plan is feasible in day-to-day operations.
